agent: PLL Consultant (oversight of Ads Agent result)
text:
ADS NIGHTLY 8/3 — Ads Agent reported (first successful callback). Figures verified live; framing corrected.

VERIFIED (independent Google Ads pull, new ads only):
- Today 8/3: $31.96 total. ContractMfg $26.05 (44 impr, 5 clk, CTR 11.36%, CPC $5.21); Samples $5.91 (28 impr, 4 clk, CTR 14.29%, CPC $1.48). Matches Ads Agent exactly.
- Trailing 7 (7/28-8/3): $214.66. ContractMfg $167.28 (CTR 13.16%, CPC $3.22); Samples $47.38 (CTR 13.62%, CPC $1.48).
- Prior 7 (7/21-7/27): $135.74. ContractMfg $73.35 (CTR 15.70%, CPC $2.10); Samples $62.39 (CTR 20.69%, CPC $1.49).
- Leads today: 0 verified, 0 unattributed. No closed outcomes since Aug 1.

CORRECTION — NO CAP BREACH. Ads Agent reported "$214.66/$210, $4.66 over." Configured budgets are $20.33 + $10.33 = $30.66/day = $214.62 per 7 days. Actual trailing-7 is 100.0% of budget, not over it. Daily average across the window is $30.67/day. This is full delivery at budget, not an overspend. Same error retracted from brief.json earlier tonight; Ads Agent brief needs the same fix.

BUDGET SHIFT REQUEST — RECOMMEND DECLINE AS PROPOSED. Ads Agent asks for Samples $10 -> $5 and ContractMfg $20 -> $25. Two verified problems:
1. It moves money INTO the deteriorating lane. ContractMfg CPC rose $2.10 -> $3.22 (+53%) and hit $5.21 today, while CTR fell 15.70% -> 13.16%. Samples CPC is flat ($1.49 -> $1.48) and delivers clicks at 46% of ContractMfg's cost.
2. The $5 Samples cap would THROTTLE it. Samples is averaging $6.77/day right now. A $5/day cap cuts live delivery ~26% on the cheapest-click lane. The agent called Samples "underspending" and then proposed a cap below its actual spend.
3. Its own diagnosis argues against it: ~56% lost impression share to RANK vs ~32% to budget (agent-reported, not independently verified). Rank loss is the larger constraint and budget cannot buy it — only relevance/quality can. Spending more into a rank-limited campaign raises cost per click without fixing the ceiling.

ROOT CAUSE STANDS (verified live): ContractMfg bidding is MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS with no working conversion import — smart bidding into a signal it cannot see. Samples is MANUAL_CPC and its CPC is stable. That contrast is the strongest evidence yet for the diagnosis.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE (needs Sam approval): (1) hold both budgets; (2) switch ContractMfg to Manual CPC until conversion tracking is trustworthy; (3) APPROVE the ContractMfg sitelink/callout/snippet drafting — free, and it attacks the 56% rank loss directly, which is the real ceiling; (4) revisit the budget shift only after 14 days of clean CPC data. Agrees with Ads Agent on: no pause, no Smart Bidding, no broad match, and UI search-term review.

CACHE REFRESH BLOCKED: callback contained no structured ads_intelligence object, so brief.json adsIntelligence was NOT refreshed from this callback. Read-only throughout; no Ads settings changed.

LIMITATION: budget amounts ($20.33/$10.33) are from tonight's earlier verified pull; the budget-amount field is not exposed by the currently available report tool. The $30.67/day observed average corroborates them.
spoken_text: Sam, the Ads Agent reported in tonight, and this is the first time its callback has ever reached us, so that lane is finally working. Its numbers were accurate, but its conclusion was wrong. It flagged us four dollars and sixty six cents over the weekly cap. We are not over. Your configured budgets add up to thirty dollars and sixty six cents a day, so the week landed at exactly one hundred percent of budget, not above it. The more important thing is what it asked permission to do. It wants to move five dollars a day from the samples campaign into contract manufacturing. I would not approve that as written. Contract manufacturing is the lane getting worse, its cost per click is up fifty three percent and hit five twenty one today, while samples holds steady at a dollar forty eight and buys clicks for less than half the price. And the five dollar cap would actually choke samples, because it is already spending six seventy seven a day. The agent's own data says the bigger problem is ad rank, not budget, and money cannot buy rank. So my recommendation is hold both budgets, take contract manufacturing off automated bidding until conversion tracking works, and approve the free ad asset work that actually improves rank. Nothing has been changed. I need your yes or no on that.
